topic: Can the triangular grid with 15% larger spacing introduce scan angle limitations or grating lobes in dense satellite constellations?
consensus_response: The triangular grid with 15% larger spacing introduces scan angle limitations due to grating lobes, as demonstrated by the rotation of the lattice by 45° compared to a square one. This affects the array factor and interference patterns, compromising capacity due to limited scan angle range. The increased spacing reduces the number of elements in the array but comes at the cost of reduced performance. Mutual coupling between closely spaced satellites exacerbates grating lobes, further affecting the overall performance.
reference_context: A triangular grid allows 15% larger spacing between unit cells compared to a rectangular grid for achieving the same maximum scan angle without grating lobes, enabling reducing the number of elements in the array and cost.
